title: Power Automate: bring your own connection in attended and unattended cloud-triggered desktop flow runs
summary: The roadmap details and maker-side embedding instructions are supported. Hold because the briefing understates documented platform controls and says the future embedding requirement is unknown even though the roadmap explicitly plans to remove it.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans bring your own connections for shared desktop flows containing connector operations in attended and unattended cloud-triggered runs.
claims.quote: This functionality allows you to bring your own connections in shared desktop flows that include connector operations and need to run in attended or unattended mode

claims.claim: The planned capability eliminates the need for embedded connection references in cloud runs.
claims.quote: eliminating the need for embedded connection references in cloud runs.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: March CY2027 is the roadmap target, not a committed release date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The listed release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new capability's default state or what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered desktop flows licensing default tenant environment setting. Read roadmap, cloudconnectors, sharing and use-connector-actions; none states the cloud BYOC default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licensing model, extra licence, price or meter specific to this new BYOC capability is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered desktop flows licensing default tenant environment setting. Read cloudconnectors and Power Automate licensing/types; neither publishes a cloud BYOC-specific licence, price or meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cloud-connectors Learn page says premium connectors require an Attended RPA licence.
claims.quote: To use premium connectors, you need an Attended RPA license.
claims.fix: Retain the attribution, but add: 'The current licence-types page names the user plan Power Automate Premium and documents Process licensing or pay-as-you-go for unattended desktop flows.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cloud-connectors page says a free work or school account can access standard connectors.
claims.quote: If you have a free work or school account, you can access standard connectors.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Embedding is configured in Power Automate through desktop flow > Details > Connection references > Manage > Embedded in desktop flow.
claims.quote: Select the desktop flow in Power Automate (make.powerautomate.com), and then select Details. ... In the Connection references section, select Manage. ... Set the Embedded in desktop flow option to Yes to enable it.

claims.claim: No API for the desktop-flow connection-reference embedding setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flow" "embedded" "connection" API workflow clientdata; "desktop flow" "embedded" "connection references" "Web API". Read cloudconnectors, desktop-flow-public-apis and Dataverse connectionreference Web API reference; none documents the embedding operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or environment switch for cloud-run BYOC is documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own" "tenant"; "bring your own connection" "cloud" "admin" Power Platform API pac PowerShell. Read cloudconnectors and desktop-flow-public-apis; results include pac admin and PowerShell overview but no cloud BYOC switch.

claims.claim: The documented embedding procedure is available to owners and co-owners.
claims.quote: To embed a connection reference to a flow that you can access as an owner or co-owner:

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: You can embed or remove a connection reference only when you own its underlying connection.
claims.quote: You can only embed or remove connection references from a desktop flow if you own the underlying connection.

claims.claim: Other co-owners can manage only connection references they added.
claims.quote: Other co-owners can only manage connection references they add.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Current documentation requires the Power Automate v2 schema to invoke a desktop flow containing connector actions from a cloud flow.
claims.quote: To successfully invoke a desktop flow containing connector actions from a cloud flow, it must meet the following two requirements: ... The desktop flow must use the Power Automate v2 schema.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Why it matters
claims.claim: Current documentation requires all connection references to be embedded for a co-owner's cloud-initiated run.
claims.quote: If you're a co-owner of the flow, all of its connection references must be marked as embedded.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Embedding permits other co-owners to access the underlying connection's data while modifying or running the shared desktop flow.
claims.quote: By embedding a connection reference to a desktop flow, you allow other co-owners to have access to the underlying data provided by it, for both modifying as well as running the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Embedded connection references are available to other co-owners only within the shared desktop flow's scope.
claims.quote: Embedded connection references are only available to other co-owners in the scope of the shared desktop flow.

claims.claim: Current documentation limits run-only users of these shared flows to console-initiated runs with their own connections.
claims.quote: Users (run-only) can run flows shared with them only via Power Automate for desktop's console using their own connections.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Each connection is specific to a user.
claims.quote: Each connection is specific to a user and requires authentication to ensure secure access to data and services.

claims.claim: Connections require authentication, typically OAuth, API keys or another service-provided method.
claims.quote: This authentication is typically done using OAuth, API keys, or other authentication methods provided by the external service.

claims.claim: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically grant access to its underlying connections.
claims.quote: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically provide access to the underlying connections utilized.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector actions access data and perform actions through the authenticated connection and its account.
claims.quote: This connection allows Power Automate to access and perform actions on data from various services, such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, SQL Server, and many others. Each connection is specific to a user

claims.claim: Importing a desktop flow with embedded references in a solution does not automatically include the required connection references.
claims.quote: When importing a desktop flow with embedded connection references in a solution, the required connection references aren't automatically included.

claims.claim: Microsoft's documented workaround is to include the required connection references explicitly in the solution.
claims.quote: To work around this current limitation, explicitly include the required connection references in the solution alongside the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Default desktop-flow connectors include Microsoft Dataverse, SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook and Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Power Automate for desktop adds these cloud connectors to desktop flows by default. You always see them in the actions pane: ... Microsoft Dataverse ... SharePoint ... Microsoft Teams ... Office 365 Outlook

claims.claim: Other non-custom Power Automate cloud connectors can be added through the Assets library.
claims.quote: To add other non-custom Power Automate cloud connectors to a desktop flow, use the Assets library.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the newly planned cloud-triggered BYOC capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated"; Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered desktop flows licensing default tenant environment setting. Read cloudconnectors and sharing; both document console BYOC instead.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which user's connector connection a new cloud BYOC run selects or who chooses it.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated". Read roadmap, cloudconnectors, sharing, use-connector-actions and desktop-flow-public-apis; none explains selection of connector connections for the new capability.

claims.claim: Storage and prompting mechanics for connector connections in unattended cloud BYOC runs are not described.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered desktop flows licensing default tenant environment setting; "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated". Read cloudconnectors and sharing; prompting is documented for console runs only.

claims.claim: No source states that existing flows automatically change behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate bring your own connection attended unattended cloud triggered desktop flows licensing default tenant environment setting. Read roadmap, cloudconnectors and sharing; no automatic migration or change to existing flows is specified.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no licence, meter or price.
claims.quote: This functionality allows you to bring your own connections in shared desktop flows that include connector operations and need to run in attended or unattended mode, eliminating the need for embedded connection references in cloud runs.

claims.claim: Data policies exist for desktop flows.
claims.quote: Power Automate offers administrators the option to create and enforce policies that classify desktop flows action groups as business or non-business and mark actions or action groups as blocked.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/data-loss-prevention for the existing desktop-flow data-policy statement.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed how general data policies apply to desktop flows using the new capability.
claims.quote: For cases that a desktop flow is suspended, it won't be able to run it. Similarly, a cloud flow using a suspend desktop flow won't be able to run either.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of Governance controls with: 'Existing desktop-flow data policies classify or block action groups; a desktop flow suspended for a policy violation cannot run, including through a cloud flow.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/data-loss-prevention.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Maker-side embedding is the only related control documented today.
claims.quote: You can use the following registry entry to disable the execution of flows containing cloud connectors. ... DisableCloudConnectors ... 1: The machine can't run desktop flows containing cloud connectors.
claims.fix: In Risk assessment, remove ', so the maker-side embedding setting is the only related control documented'. In Governance controls, change 'The one related control documented today is maker-side' to 'The embedding control is maker-side'. This removes the false exclusivity without adding a control row.

claims.claim: The new capability's connector coverage is not specified.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated". Read roadmap and cloudconnectors; the roadmap says connector operations without a coverage list, and Learn lists current desktop-flow connectors rather than coverage for the new feature.

claims.claim: Whether the Power Automate v2 schema requirement remains for the new capability is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated". Read roadmap, cloudconnectors and sharing; the v2 requirement is documented for current cloud runs, but no source discusses its future under cloud BYOC.

claims.where: Scope: 'Whether those prerequisites stay is not stated'
claims.claim: Whether embedded connection references remain a prerequisite under cloud BYOC is not stated.
claims.quote: eliminating the need for embedded connection references in cloud runs.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether those prerequisites stay is not stated' with: 'The roadmap plans to remove the embedded-reference requirement; whether the Power Automate v2 schema requirement remains is not stated.'

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether cloud BYOC changes the solution-import limitation.
claims.quote: Searched: "desktop flows" "bring your own connection" "cloud-initiated"; "desktop flow" "embedded" "connection references" "Web API". Read roadmap and sharing; the import limitation is documented without any discussion of the planned capability.

claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to review data policies, but the controls table has no data-policy row.
claims.quote: Re-check how data policies apply to connector actions in desktop flows once Microsoft documents the feature. ... controls: connection-reference embedding; tenant or environment BYOC switch.
claims.fix: The After rollout data-policy checklist step has no matching controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
